0|3bf5ee95648c694bac4d13529563c230cd4fe5f2|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"[PATCH] freepgt: hugetlb_free_pgd_range
ia64 and ppc64 had hugetlb_free_pgtables functions which were no longer being
called
column2: and it wasn't obvious what to do about them.

column1: The ppc64 case turns out to be easy: the associated tables are noted elsewhere
and freed later
column2: safe to either skip its hugetlb areas or go through the

column1: motions of freeing nothing.  Since ia64 does need a special case
ppc64 the special case of skipping them.
The ia64 hugetlb case has been broken since pgd_addr_end went in
probably appeared to work okay if you just had one such area; in fact it's
been broken much longer if you consider a long munmap spanning from another
region into the hugetlb region.
In the ia64 hugetlb region
column2: more virtual address bits are available than in

column1: the other regions
column2: yet the page tables are structured the same way: the page

column1: at the bottom is larger.  Here we need to scale down each addr before passing
it to the standard free_pgd_range.  Was about to write a hugely_scaled_down
macro
column2: but found htlbpage_to_page already exists for just this purpose.  Fixed

column1: off-by-one in ia64 is_hugepage_only_range.
Uninline free_pgd_range to make it available to ia64.  Make sure the
vma-gathering loop in free_pgtables cannot join a hugepage_only_range to any
other (safe to join huges?  probably but don't bother).
